answer: Submissions from one IP or ASN within a short time window share a shrinking payout, so a farm behind a single exit cannot scale its yield. The ledger scores a kernel density over source addresses and timestamps; when many answers surface from one marble-smooth network block at once, each added identity earns progressively less. A whisper of separation in route or hour resets the curve. Attacker cost: a distinct egress per identity or staggered timing, neither cheap for a centralized botnet.
